Anexo Parte I 1.6 (PDF p. 8): limits apply to the product in the state in which it is offered to the consumer; 1.5: to the edible part; 2.4 (PDF p. 9): for fish and fishery products, to the product as consumed eviscerated, without head and thorax where applicable; 2.7: limits expressed in mg/kg. GMC 18/21), which modifies only the rice row ('Arroz y sus derivados excepto aceite') of the arsenic table; this row is unchanged. Row has no url in the register; raw path located via raw/regulatory search.

rows.scope: Schedule 19, S19-4 'Maximum levels of metal contaminants' table: contaminant 'Arsenic (inorganic)', food 'Seaweed'
rows.basis: S19-4: maximum level in mg/kg; S19-3(1)(b): for a food for which only a portion is ordinarily consumed, a reference to the food is a reference to that portion; S19-3(1)(c): in the case of seaweed, calculations are to be based on seaweed at 85% hydration
rows.evidence: "Arsenic (inorganic) ... Seaweed 1" — S19-4 table, Authorised Version F2024C00908, p. 2
rows.primary_source_used: /Users/karenpendergrass/Desktop/heavy-metal-index/raw/regulatory/au-nz/au-nz-fsanz-standard-1-4-1-schedule-19.pdf (Authorised Version F2024C00908, compilation No. 6 as in force on 13 September 2024, registered 21/10/2024); currency cross-checked at https://www.legislation.gov.au/F2015L00454/latest/versions and https://api.prod.legislation.gov.au/v1/titles/F2026L01125
rows.note: 1 mg/kg x 1000 = 1000 ug/kg. Held copy is compilation No. 6 (F2024C00908) as in force on 13 September 2024; legislation.gov.au lists it as the latest compilation (period 13 Sep 2024 - 31 Aug 2026). The only later amendment is Variation F2026L01125 (Application A1329, exclusion of Blacklip Rock oysters farmed in the Northern Territory from the cadmium ML for molluscs; made 20 Aug 2026, registered 28 Aug 2026, commenced 1 Sep 2026), which is scoped to cadmium in molluscs and does not touch the arsenic/seaweed entry; no C07 compilation was registered as of 2026-09-02. Register basis 'portion ordinarily consumed' is consistent with S19-3(1)(b) but omits the seaweed-specific 85% hydration basis in S19-3(1)(c), which a reader converting dry seaweed data would need.
